prompt:
SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired sprite sheet for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up: the LASER — a piercing beam: a blazing white core blade inside a narrow cyan sheath with tip spark.

Design identity to keep exactly — Retro 16-bit player projectile detail: crisp two-tone energy look, bright core, navy outline, tiny specular spark — clearly a forward-flying weapon (nose right).

Rebuild it as a sprite sheet under this strict contract:
- On a CONTINUOUS flat pure bright green chroma-key background, exactly hex #51e018, identical solid colour in every background pixel: no gradient, no vignette, no shadow, no floor plane, no panel, no second green shade.
- The sheet holds exactly ONE cell — the WHOLE canvas is the single subject's frame; an empty sheet ruins it.
- Cells in reading order (left-right, then top-bottom):
  cell 1 = the beam pointing right The subject fills the cell as ONE large centred figure, aspect ratio about 2.6:1 (1.8:1 to 3.6:1).
- The sheet canvas measures EXACTLY 576×256 px. Produce EXACTLY 1 subject cell — no more, no fewer — and nothing else on the sheet.
- Each subject sits well inside its cell with at least 20 px of unbroken flat #51e018 around it and clean flat gutters between cells: no subject may touch or cross a cell edge; keep every subject within the inner 75% of its cell.
- NO guide lines, NO cell borders, NO divider lines, NO frames, NO text, NO labels, NO numbers anywhere on the sheet — the cell names above are ordering instructions and must NEVER be drawn.
- Style: retro 16-bit pixel art, chunky visible square pixels, flat saturated fills with a three-step shading ramp lit from the top-left, crisp 1-px near-black navy outline on every silhouette edge, no anti-aliasing, no motion blur.
negative: photorealistic, 3d render, text, labels, numbers, cell borders, guide lines, grid lines, watermark, blurry, anti-aliasing, gradient background, scenery, stars, cast shadow, multiple subjects per cell, empty cell
